The 10 other failures are environment-only and fail identically on untouched master in the planning container (test_events_nats_consumer x6: nats-py not installed; test_aider_harness_availability x2: proxy-injected GH_TOKEN; test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path: the container HOME is banned by value; test_remote_sync ssh: no ssh binary). 0 conflicts for this story.

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHY: ADR 0011 decision 3: a state change enqueues "advance plan X", and requests for the same plan coalesce while one is queued. This story builds the queue only; SQ-06 wires it into the daemon.

WHAT TO BUILD: NEW pipeline/advance_queue.py with class `AdvanceQueue` (thread-safe, one `threading.Condition`):
- `request(plan_name: str, reason: str = "") -> bool`: a non-str `plan_name` raises TypeError (ruff TRY004 rejects a ValueError there); a str is validated with `pipeline.parsers._validate_key` (raise ValueError naming the argument, never echoing the value). If the plan is already queued, return False (coalesced). If it is in flight (taken, not yet finished), mark it dirty and return False. Otherwise append it FIFO and return True.
- `take(timeout_s: float | None) -> str | None`: block until a plan is queued or the timeout expires (None means wait forever); move it from queued to in-flight and return it. Returns None on timeout or after `close()`.
- `finish(plan_name: str) -> None`: remove it from in-flight and record `time.monotonic()` as its last-advanced time. If it was marked dirty while in flight, clear the mark and re-append it at the TAIL (fairness: it goes behind plans already waiting). Finishing a plan that is not in flight is a no-op that logs at DEBUG.
- `last_advanced(plan_name: str) -> float | None` and `close()` (wakes all waiters; later `take` returns None, later `request` returns False).
No other public API. No persistence: the queue is in-process state; the reconcile sweep (SQ-06) refills it after a restart.

- FIFO order across three plans.
- A second request for a queued plan returns False and the plan is taken once.
- A request while in flight returns False; after `finish` the plan is queued again behind a plan requested meanwhile.
- `finish` without a dirty mark does not re-queue; `last_advanced` is set.
- `take(0.05)` on an empty queue returns None within 1 s.
- A blocked `take(None)` on another thread returns the plan after `request` (join the thread with a timeout).
- `close()` releases a blocked `take` with None, and `request` after close returns False.
- Invalid names (`""`, `"../x"`) raise ValueError and a non-str raises TypeError; neither message contains the value.

stories.description: ADR 0011 S1. A worker process advances many plans one after another, paying the ~1 s pipeline import once instead of once per plan.

WHY: pipeline/advance_one.py runs exactly one plan per process; importing `pipeline.server` costs 0.9-1.4 s. Advancing plans ONE AT A TIME in a persistent process is safe even though `REPO_ROOT` is a process global, because `_scoped_repo_root` swaps and restores it per advance, exactly as the serial in-process loop does today. Only concurrent advances in one process are unsafe, and this worker never runs two at once.

1. pipeline/advance_one.py: extract the per-process setup in `main` (logging, `_apply_scheduler_role_call_clamp`, the `service.instance.id` resource attribute, `telemetry.configure()` / `configure_metrics()`) into `configure_child() -> None` and call it from `main`. Behaviour of `main` is unchanged; its existing tests must stay green without edits.
2. NEW pipeline/advance_worker.py, run as `python -m pipeline.advance_worker <in_fd> <out_fd>`:

stories.summary: Add a supervised pool of long-lived advance workers
stories.description: ADR 0011 S1. Threads in the scheduler hand queued plans to persistent worker processes, with a per-plan timeout that kills and respawns a stuck worker.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-29 on master 2f76447 - a stand-in of SQ-01..15 applied together: 18569 passed / 51 skipped, ruff and the line-limit gate clean. The 10 other failures are environment-only and fail identically on untouched master in the planning container (test_events_nats_consumer x6: nats-py not installed; test_aider_harness_availability x2: proxy-injected GH_TOKEN; test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path: the container HOME is banned by value; test_remote_sync ssh: no ssh binary). 0 conflicts for this story.

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHY: the pooled reconcile waits for EVERY child before the pass ends, so the slowest plan in the fleet sets every plan's latency. Long-lived workers fed from the SQ-03 queue let each plan go round again as soon as its own advance finishes.

WHAT TO BUILD: NEW pipeline/advance_workers.py with class `AdvanceWorkerPool(size: int, queue: AdvanceQueue, plan_timeout_s: Callable[[], float])`:
- `start()`: start `size` daemon threads named `advance-worker-<n>`. Each thread owns at most one child at a time: `python -m pipeline.advance_worker <in_fd> <out_fd>` started with `subprocess.Popen(..., pass_fds=(child_in_read, child_out_write), cwd=_source_root(), stdin=DEVNULL, stdout=DEVNULL)`, closing the child's ends in the parent after the spawn. Children inherit the parent's process group (no `start_new_session`): agents they launch must survive them, as in pipeline/advance_pool.py.
- Thread loop: `plan = queue.take(1.0)`; None -> loop (exit when stopping). Otherwise ensure a live child (spawn if none or if `poll()` is not None), write `{"plan": plan}\n`, then wait for one result line with `select` on the out pipe bounded by `plan_timeout_s()` (read per advance, so an operator override applies without a restart). Always call `queue.finish(plan)` in a `finally`.

WHY: SQ-13 can fetch every open PR's checks in one call. 1. pipeline/forge_github.py `checks_snapshot(branch, sha)`: when `sha` is non-empty and `PIPELINE_CI_ROLLUP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (default 90; `0` disables; malformed, non-finite or negative logs a WARNING and uses 90) is positive, return `ci_rollup.cached_snapshot(<scoped repo root>, sha, <state root>, max_age)` when it is not None; otherwise run today's REST call unchanged. The state root follows the rule pipeline/detached_grade.py uses (`PIPELINE_STATE_DIR`, else the manifests base); put that resolution in ci_rollup.py if it is not already importable. A cache hit must never turn a sha that REST would report as failing into a pass: the cache only ever holds what GitHub reported, and a stale entry is ignored.
2. pipeline/watchers.py `scan_all_plans`: collect `repo_root -> [(plan, story_key, ci_pending_sha)]` for every `pr_open` story with a `ci_pending_sha` (the field pipeline/advance_merge.py sets while CI is pending). The whole step is wrapped so it can never break the scan.
3. REFERENCE.md rows for `PIPELINE_CI_ROLLUP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` and `PIPELINE_CI_ROLLUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` next to the CI gate settings, stating the GraphQL budget: one query per repository with pending PRs per interval (120 per hour per repository at the default).
